text:
sara: Hey team — customer on free tier hit a series of 429s during a live demo. They say things worked fine earlier but around 11:37am PST their ingest job burst and started getting immediate throttles. Need quick guidance: can we grant a short burst allowance or advise on a repro/fix? :eyes:

alex: Can you paste the exact 429 response headers/log snippet? Important to know whether this is per-minute tokens, concurrency, or connection-level concurrency.

sara: Pasting log from customer (redacted keys):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 14 Jan 2025 19:37:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 1705235832
Retry-After: 45
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "Rate limit exceeded: free plan per-minute cap"
}
```
They also sent their client repro: a simple loop of concurrent embedding calls (5 parallel workers) hitting /v1/embeddings for ~200 short items.

priya: That header set looks like a per-minute cap (limit=60). The Retry-After 45s confirms backoff response. If they ran 5 concurrent workers without pacing they'd easily burn through quick bursts.

sara: Yep. Customer wants either a temporary bump for a 1-hour demo or a fast path to a paid starter so this doesn't block the sales demo.

kevin: @sara I can take this — we have a small temporary burst pool for demos but it's sales-assisted. Can you share org_id and the demo start/end window? I can route a one-time 2x cap for 90 minutes if ops gives the green light.

ops-oncall: Quick note — we prefer not to change global caps without approval. If it's a one-off, make sure the customer follows these repro mitigation steps first: exponential backoff with jitter, request batching (bulk embeddings call), or serialize the workers to <=2 concurrent. Also advise adding a small client-side token bucket.

sara: Repro steps I sent to them (curl example):
```
# bad pattern (burns quota instantly)
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"open-embedding-1","input":"hello"}' &
done
wait
\n# recommended: serialized with simple retry
for i in {1..200}; do
  attempt=0
  until [ "$attempt" -ge 5 ] || curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"open-embedding-1","input":"hello"}' ; do
    attempt=$((attempt+1))
    sleep $((2 ** attempt + (RANDOM % 3)))
  done
done
```

kevin: Thanks. @ops-oncall — can we make an exception? If ops approves, I'll send a one-hour temporary increase (2x per-minute) and CC billing for tracking. Customer org: org_9b7c (demo window 2025-01-14 18:50–20:20 UTC).

ops-oncall: I can approve a scoped increase if it's limited to that org and auto-reverts. Two checks: (1) confirm they don't have a linked paid contract already, (2) ensure we log the change and notify infra.

billing-bot: Automated note: No active paid subscription found for org_9b7c. Creating internal ticket BILL-2025-311 for audit trail.

sara: Customer accepted the mitigation steps and asked to proceed with temporary bump while they prep a paid trial. I'll attach the repro artifacts and customer contact.

alex: From an engineering side, also recommend they set the header X-RW-CLIENT-ID (app-level) so we can do targeted tracing if throttles continue. If they keep hitting 429s after a temporary bump, ask them to share that header and a sequence of X-Request-Id traces and we can map requests.

kevin: I put through the request and ops approved the 90-minute 2x cap for org_9b7c — auto-revert in 95 minutes. Sent the confirmation to the customer and CC'd billing. :white_check_mark:

sara: Closing loop — customer ran the demo successfully after we applied the bump and implemented the serialized retry. They want a follow-up on upgrade options. @kevin can you take the handoff for pricing?

kevin: On it. I'll schedule a short call and share Starter plan options with a recommended concurrency profile for embeddings (start at 500/min).

priya: FYI for docs: we should add a short checklist for demos in the public support KB: "pre-demo checklist: tag requests with X-RW-CLIENT-ID, limit concurrency, batch embeddings, and request temporary demo burst by contacting sales@redwood.ai".

sara: Thanks all. Filing internal notes and the customer is unblocked. :tada:
